articles.title: A Simple Harmattan Dust Routine for Busy Homes
articles.excerpt: Fine dust on every surface? A 15-minute daily routine that keeps it under control.

body.p: Harmattan season brings a fine layer of dust that settles on everything. The trick is little and often, rather than one big clean at the weekend.
Dust falls, so clean shelves and window ledges first, then tables, then the floor.
A dry cloth just moves dust around. Use a microfibre cloth lightly sprayed with Multi-Surface Cleaner to trap it.

list: Close louvres during the windiest hours

articles.title: How to Get Palm-Oil Stains Off Pots and Plastic Bowls
articles.excerpt: That orange tint on your plastic bowls doesn't have to be permanent.

body.p: Palm oil is delicious but stubborn. Here's how to lift it from pots, bowls and containers.
Use a paper towel to wipe out as much oil as possible before washing. Less oil means less soap.
Add a little Multipurpose Liquid Soap to warm water and soak for 15 minutes, then scrub.
For plastic bowls with an orange tint, dry them in direct sunlight after washing. The colour often fades.

articles.title: Keeping White School Uniforms Bright All Term
articles.excerpt: Collars, cuffs and red-earth stains — our tested tips for brighter whites.

body.p: White uniforms take a beating. A little care each week keeps them looking new for longer.
Rub a little Multipurpose Liquid Soap into collars and cuffs and leave for 10 minutes before washing.
Soak in cool water with a capful of Multipurpose Liquid Soap. Hot water can set some stains.

list: Dry in the sun, inside out

articles.title: The 10-Minute Bathroom Grout & Limescale Refresh
articles.excerpt: Dark grout lines make a clean bathroom look dirty. Here's a quick fix.

body.p: Grout is porous, so it holds on to soap and dirt. A weekly refresh keeps it light.

list: Apply diluted Stain Remover along the grout lines (gloves on, window open)
Open a window to let the room air out

body.p: Never mix Stain Remover or any acid cleaner with bleach — the fumes can be dangerous.

articles.title: Why Buying Big Sizes and Refills Saves You Money
articles.excerpt: The maths behind refilling, explained simply.

body.p: Small bottles cost more per litre. When you buy a 5L or 25L jug and refill the bottles you already own, you pay for cleaner, not packaging.
Compare the price per litre on each size. The bigger jugs usually work out cheapest.

articles.title: Safe Cleaning Habits When You Have Young Children
articles.excerpt: Simple storage and cleaning habits for a home with little ones.

body.p: Whatever products you use, a few simple habits make your home safer for children.

list: Store cleaners up high or in a locked cupboard
Keep products in their original labelled bottles
Never pour cleaners into drink bottles
Keep Ghana's emergency number (112) and your doctor's number handy

body.p: Read the label of every product before use, and follow its directions and warnings.
